shots.composition_notes: Opens on a symmetrical wide shot of the restaurant with the two leads dead-center and small in frame, flanked by mirrored rows of tables/chandeliers and a title card (episode number + one-word verdict) burned over the top third. Camera pushes in steadily over ~2s, tightening from the full dining room down to a medium close-up on the man's face reading the menu; his glasses and nose stay locked on the vertical center line the whole time, headroom shrinking as the push continues. Background diners stay symmetrically arranged left/right and go soft with depth of field as the lens tightens.

Locked-off close-up on the woman, centered on her nose/eyeline with the wine glass anchoring the lower-left third and her closed menu resting on the table edge. Caption word ("MENU") sits at chin height. Background chandelier/sconce and blurred diners stay mirrored behind her, same shallow-DOF treatment as prior shot but no further camera movement.

Hard cut to an extreme close-up insert on the menu itself: his torso and chin fill the top of frame (nose and mouth only, eyes cropped out entirely), hands frame the open menu left and right in near-perfect symmetry, water glass and wine glass just visible at the outer edges. Static, tripod-locked framing used purely to let the on-screen caption words ("HAS", "ON", "TRUFFLE") land as isolated punchline beats.

Returns to the same locked close-up crop on the woman used in the earlier reverse shot (same eyeline, same wine-glass foreground element), reinforcing a clean shot-reverse-shot pattern rather than introducing a new angle. Brief scene (~1.2s) with no camera movement.

Cuts to a tight, static close-up on the man, cropped from forehead to mouth so his oversized nose and round glasses dominate the center of frame; caption ("I'M" / "$29") sits directly over his mouth. Eyebrows lower into an angry V as the beat lands, but the framing itself never moves — all the escalation is in the puppet's expression, not the camera.

Final reaction shot on the woman, a hair wider than her earlier close-ups so her pearl earrings and collar are visible, still centered and static with the same blurred symmetrical restaurant background. Caption "FAMOUS" lands at chin height, matching the caption-placement convention used in every prior shot.

End card: solid black background, centered serif title "LOW BATTERY PEOPLE" / "CREATED BY NIN." with a small yellow "NEW EPISODE DAILY" ribbon graphic beneath, all elements horizontally centered. Pure static graphic, no camera motion or set.

framing_patterns_notes: Strict shot-reverse-shot alternation between two static, centered close-ups (man vs. woman), always with the puppet's nose/eyeline on the frame's vertical center and the blurred restaurant symmetrically arranged behind them — the only camera movement in the whole piece is the single opening push-in from the wide establishing shot into the first close-up. The one exception to the close-up pattern is a static extreme close-up insert on the menu/hands used as a punctuation beat for the joke's key words. Every caption word is burned at the same vertical position (roughly chin/collar height) regardless of shot type, so the text placement, not the camera, is what visually unifies the cuts.
